brief.summary: VERIFIED ground truth (re-checked live + on-disk): oyatie's CI/CD lives in two DISJOINT git worlds with NO merge-base — github-mirror/dev (9f1047e62, 10 commits, LIVE on GitHub, carries ONLY the lane-unlocker workflow) and phase0/producer (2deaa3bcd, 985 commits, checked out on disk, carries the firewall+gates+oya-ci-controller). Go-live (ADD oya-ci-required ALONGSIDE github-lane-unlocker-required, zero-regression) is therefore a fresh-root IMPORT, not a merge/cherry-pick. The current LIVE state is a stack of false-greens that DIRECTLY violate the founder's 4 directives: (1) BEST-PRACTICE VIOLATION — live branch protection is the INVERSE of the repo's own committed SSOT: live requires the single context github-lane-unlocker-required (which the committed branch-protection.yaml:40 explicitly labels 'shadow compatibility only ... must not be treated as merge authority'), while the committed SSOT declares oya-ci-required as authority with enforce_admins:true + required_signatures:true; LIVE has enforce_admins:false, required_signatures:false — admins bypass and unsigned commits merge. A second drift: live required_approving_review_count=1 (verified via the .../required_pull_request_reviews sub-endpoint; the top-level protection JSON omits the object) contradicts the committed dev.json:16 (null) and the agent-run-review doctrine — a human approval is silently a live merge gate. (3) SURFACE-ALL VIOLATION — the ONLY blocking job (github-lane-unlocker-required 'Aggregate bridge evidence', workflow lines 79-87) re-runs only 7 governance targets under one bash -e run: block, so the FIRST failing buck2 build aborts the step (fail-fast) AND it OMITS buck2-authority-policy-check, buck2-cargo-target-coverage-check, rust-llvm-coverage-*, and infra/ci/buck2-affected-gate.sh — a structural false-green where a failing fanout lane need not block. The collect-ALL property (evaluate_keyed → BTreeSet, no early return; firewall compare() loops union of keys with no early exit, lib.rs:168-215) EXISTS but is library-only (cloud-ci-firewall has NO main.rs/bin) and wired into ZERO pipelines. (4) AUTOMATE/DRIFT VIOLATION — staleness-reaper runs nowhere; nothing diffs live gh protection vs committed dev.json (the inversion above is itself undetected drift); no merge queue (gh rulesets=[], no merge_group), no postsubmit/periodic/cron, no signing/provenance live. (2) THROUGHPUT — the live gate has NO cache (.buckconfig has only [cells]/[build], no RE/action-cache stanza; bootstrap reinstalls rustup+buck2 every run) and the producer pays a ~12s/run O(paths×file-size) reachability scan (~12.45 GB scanned) at main.rs:614 — the O(1) token-index fix is ALREADY proven in-tree at resolve_justifications (main.rs:678). The firewall predicate design itself is sound (block-on-new + shrink-only ratchet + EMPTY founder-signed signoff = ratchet fully closed) — it just is not wired anywhere. The brutal-honest bottom line: there is currently NO true blocking CI gate on dev that runs the firewall or surfaces all failures; the one required check is a narrow, fail-fast, false-green subset re-run, enforced by a protection config that inverts its own committed source.
best_practices: One required context, App-posted, that is a PURE zero-build fan-in (needs: [all-lanes], exit 0) — the required check is green IFF every fanout lane is green; it must NEVER run its own narrower command set (the current required job re-runs 7 governance targets and omits authority/coverage/affected, a structural false-green).

Branch-protection-as-code with a presubmit drift gate: store the SSOT (infra/branch-protection/dev.json + .github/branch-protection.yaml) and add a check that fetches gh api .../branches/dev/protection and BYTE-DIFFS it, failing RED on any mismatch — this single gate would have caught all three live drifts (context inversion, signatures off, admins off, review-count=1).

Four-stage pipeline split (presubmit affected-closure = blocking/fast; postsubmit whole-graph //:...-check on dev after merge; periodic nightly whole-graph + staleness-reaper + toolchain-pin = the directive-#4 backstop that fires even if presubmit drifts; release-gate = cosign/SLSA provenance + canary). Live state is presubmit-ONLY.

Surface-all aggregation as a real CI entrypoint: build cloud-ci-firewall's missing main.rs/bin that runs every gate's evaluate_keyed, aggregates into ONE FirewallReport, and writes a GitHub Check-Run with per-finding inline annotations + a single summary listing EVERY failure (the data — fixed/regression/tolerated key-sets, baseline-block-on-new vs advisory-until-infra mode — already exists in compare(), it just is not surfaced).

Block-on-new ratchet with a single founder-signed one-way-door allowlist (gate-baseline.signoff.json), baseline may only SHRINK; advisory-until-infra codes emit a visibly-shrinking burn-down dashboard rather than a permanent non-blocking footnote — turns tolerated debt into a tracked ratchet, never a silent false-green.

Supply-chain trust at the merge boundary: enforce required_signatures + enforce_admins + required_linear_history to match the committed SSOT, and move signature verification INTO the gate Run ('the signature IS the check') so it is forge-neutral and survives the planned SCM swap.

Merge queue (GitHub-native merge_group interim NOW, own Tide-invariant serial batch at oya-ci Phase-1: batches>singletons, retest-base, abort-on-HEAD-move) to close the strict:false + no-queue stale-merge hole where a green-but-stale PR can land and break dev.

Decouple WHERE oya-ci-required is PRODUCED (controller Job image, branch-agnostic, via the forge-neutral CommitStatusPoster seam) from WHERE the firewall SOURCE lives — this dissolves the disjoint-history entanglement: an App-posted status needs no shared history.

Throughput SLOs + flake policy: publish presubmit p50/p95 + queue-depth SLOs and a flake budget; implement bounded auto-retry + quarantine where the quarantine list is a DATA artifact that EMITS a burn-down (never a silent mask), so a flaky test is visibly tracked, not hidden.

brief.surface_all_design: The pipeline must SURFACE ALL via a two-level design that is parallel AT THE TOP and collect-all AT THE BOTTOM, with the required check being a pure fan-in (never a re-runner). LEVEL 1 (parallel/fast, already partly correct): the workflow matrix runs lanes with strategy.fail-fast:false + max-parallel:4 so lanes never cancel each other — KEEP this. LEVEL 2 (collect-all, the missing piece): build cloud-ci-firewall's absent main.rs/bin as the SINGLE aggregation entrypoint. It runs every gate's evaluate_keyed (each already collects ALL findings into a BTreeSet<Finding> with NO early return — verified in total-accounting/staleness-reaper/automation-ratchet/cross-artifact-agreement) and the firewall's compare() loops the UNION of all (gate,code) keys pushing a CodeReport per code with no early exit (lib.rs:168-215). A code FAILs iff mode==baseline-block-on-new AND it has NEW regression keys (lib.rs:143-145); advisory-until-infra codes emit counts but never flip the verdict; is_green = no failing code AND no un-signed-off ratchet growth (lib.rs:160-162). The bin emits ONE FirewallReport → a GitHub Check-Run with per-finding inline annotations + a single summary that lists EVERY failure across ALL gates, plus a persisted burn-down artifact for advisory codes. THE KEY FIX for fail-fast: the current blocking job runs 7 sequential `buck2 build` lines under one bash -e run: block (first failure aborts) AND the affected-gate is set -eu — both must STOP being sequential shell builds. Replace them with (a) the firewall aggregator invocation (durable), or as a stopgap `buck2 build ... --keep-going`; and (b) make the required GitHub context a ZERO-BUILD fan-in job: needs:[all-lanes] + exit 0, so it is green IFF every parallel lane is green — it must never run its own narrower command set (today's subset re-run is the structural false-green). PARALLEL + FAST is preserved because lanes fan out across runners (and, with affected-targeting + remote cache, only touched targets compile); SURFACE-ALL is guaranteed because (i) every lane runs to completion under matrix fail-fast:false, (ii) within each gate evaluate_keyed aggregates all findings, and (iii) the firewall produces one report enumerating every failure so fixes land in a single sweep. To keep surface-all at scale, the merge queue runs the same full aggregator once per BATCH (every gate still runs to completion per batch). The single-required-context choice is deliberate: it avoids the multi-producer deadlock the repo already hit (oya-pr-review HTTP 501 would have blocked every PR), while the per-finding annotations + burn-down deliver the surface-all developer UX from INSIDE the Run, not from the one-line commit-status the controller posts.

golive_topology_options.option: A — App-posted commit-status FIRST (decouple producer from source): make oya-ci-required a pure GitHub-App commit status produced by the oya-ci-controller's Job image (executing the firewall aggregator out-of-tree), then ADD it ALONGSIDE github-lane-unlocker-required after a verdict-agreement shadow period. Needs NO shared history because an App-posted status is branch-agnostic via the forge-neutral CommitStatusPoster seam.
golive_topology_options.pros: Dissolves the disjoint-history entanglement entirely (no merge/cherry-pick needed); zero-regression ADD-alongside matches the founder directive; lets RED/GREEN be proven in shadow before the ruleset flip; controller seam already exists (verified: kernel CommitStatusPoster + GitHubCommitStatusPoster adapter + controller bin wiring).
golive_topology_options.cons: oya-ci-required has no LIVE producer today (controller is shadow, not deployed), so requires the in-cluster controller (with-infra); the surface-all UX must come from inside the Job (Check-Run annotations), not the one-line 240-char commit-status the controller posts.

golive_topology_options.option: B — Thin hand-ported PR onto dev: land the firewall gates + accounting-registry-producer + cloud-ci-firewall bin onto the live dev root as a single auditable PR (fresh-root import, NOT a merge), wire cloud-ci-firewall-gate into the lane matrix, then ADD oya-ci-required.
golive_topology_options.pros: Firewall SOURCE becomes visible/auditable on dev's graph; makes oya-ci-required producible by GitHub Actions without the cluster (no controller dependency for the producer); transparent diff for review.
golive_topology_options.cons: Disjoint history (985 vs 10 commits, no merge-base) means the import is manual and lossy of provenance; risks re-introducing forbidden-vocab/stale files from phase0/producer unless filtered; larger blast radius than an App-posted status.

golive_topology_options.option: C — Promote phase0/producer to BECOME dev (default-branch swap): make the 985-commit firewall branch the new dev, retiring the 10-commit mirror.
golive_topology_options.pros: Single source of truth; no porting; the firewall and all gates are natively present.
golive_topology_options.cons: Hard one-way door requiring explicit founder sign-off on a default-branch rewrite; orphans the live mirror's history; highest blast radius; the live lane-unlocker workflow does NOT exist on phase0/producer (only backbone-microservices-ci.yml), so the live gate would have to be re-created. NOT recommended before founder go.

open_questions: Review-count reconciliation: live required_approving_review_count=1 (authoritative sub-endpoint) vs committed dev.json:16 null and the agent-run-review doctrine — is a human approval an intentional live gate, or undetected drift to be reset to 0? recommendations.action: FACET 1 — Presubmit / Postsubmit / Periodic / Release-gate (the four CI stages). RECOMMEND: presubmit = buck2 affected-closure (fast, throughput) AS the blocking gate; postsubmit = whole-graph //:...-check on dev after merge (catches affected-selection gaps, paging-but-non-blocking); periodic = nightly whole-graph + staleness-reaper + toolchain-pin refresh (the directive-#4 backstop that fires even if presubmit drifts); release-gate = provenance/cosign + canary-analysis on the tag. This is the missing 3 of 4 stages today.
recommendations.rationale: VERIFIED premise: dev tip carries ONLY github-lane-unlocker-ci-cd.yml with no schedule/cron/merge_group trigger, so the live state is presubmit-only with no periodic backstop — drift can land and sit. Affected-presubmit + whole-graph-postsubmit/periodic is the Google/Meta pattern and satisfies directives #2 (throughput) and #4 (drift impossible — periodic catches what affected-selection misses).
recommendations.throughput_impact: Large positive: presubmit shrinks from whole-graph to affected-closure; whole-graph cost moves off the critical path to postsubmit/periodic.

recommendations.action: FACET 2 — SURFACE-ALL aggregation (directive #3), the single most violated facet. RECOMMEND (b)+(c): build the missing cloud-ci-firewall main.rs/[[bin]] as the single CI entrypoint that runs every gate's evaluate_keyed, aggregates into one FirewallReport, writes a GitHub Check-Run with inline annotations per finding + one summary listing every failure, AND a burn-down artifact for advisory codes. Replace the sequential `buck2 build //:...-check` shell list in the required job with one invocation of that aggregator (or `buck2 build ... --keep-going` as a stopgap, but the aggregator is the durable fix).
recommendations.rationale: VERIFIED premise: the blocking job (github-lane-unlocker-ci-cd.yml:67-87) chains 7 buck2 builds under one bash -e run: block and dies on the first failure — structurally cannot 'surface all'; AND the affected-gate.sh is set -eu fail-fast. Meanwhile the firewall already aggregates correctly in lib.rs (compare() at :172-215 no-early-exit, is_green() at :160-162) but has NO bin (find shows only lib.rs+tests) and does not run in CI. Wiring it as the entrypoint is the direct, evidence-backed fix.
recommendations.throughput_impact: Neutral-to-positive on wall-clock; large positive on fix-throughput (one sweep instead of N round-trips).

recommendations.action: FACET 3 — Merge-queue / batching (Tide). RECOMMEND interim GitHub-native merge queue (merge_group trigger) on dev NOW (zero-build, immediate throughput + eliminates the strict:false stale-merge gap), then own Tide-invariant serial batch (batches>singletons, retest-base, abort-on-HEAD-move) at oya-ci Phase-1 with graph-exact conflicts(a,b) from the Buck2 brain; gate the Phase-3 speculation-tree behind a measured queue-p50 SLO.
recommendations.rationale: VERIFIED premise: no merge_group trigger in any workflow; strict:false in live dev protection means a green-but-stale PR can merge and break dev; ADR-0515:110 records 0124's webhook merge-queue as superseded-in-mechanism into Tide (Face A at :76) but unbuilt. A queue closes the stale-merge hole and is the canonical throughput lever (directive #2); the interim GH queue is a bridge, not a divergent decision.
recommendations.throughput_impact: Large positive: batching amortizes retest cost across PRs; closes stale-merge regressions that otherwise cost re-runs.

recommendations.action: FACET 4 — Disjoint-topology go-live for the firewall (the hardest facet; dev and phase0/producer share NO history). RECOMMEND (c) FIRST: make oya-ci-required a pure App-posted commit status — the controller already posts it via the forge-neutral CommitStatusPoster seam, executing the firewall out-of-tree in the controller's Job image, so the App-posted check needs no shared history. THEN (a) land the firewall source onto dev via a thin hand-ported PR for transparency/auditability. Explicitly NOT (b) promoting phase0/producer to become dev until the founder signs the default-branch swap (one-way door). Sequence: shadow-observe -> add oya-ci-required ALONGSIDE github-lane-unlocker-required -> port source via thin-PR.
recommendations.rationale: VERIFIED premise: `git merge-base phase0/producer github-mirror/dev` returns nonzero (disjoint, 985 vs 10 commits), so cherry-pick/merge is infeasible; the firewall is library-only (no bin) and lives only on phase0/producer. Decoupling 'where oya-ci-required is PRODUCED' (controller Job image, branch-agnostic — seam verified at kernel lib.rs:620-621 + adapter :82 + controller bin :77) from 'where the firewall SOURCE lives' dissolves the entanglement and matches the briefed zero-regression ADD-alongside cutover.
